domestic.current_account: Unchanged this run: June 2026 swung to a $649mn monthly deficit (from May's $500mn surplus), closing FY26 at a marginal $139mn full-year deficit (https://www.dawn.com/news/2016383/current-account-slips-into-139m-deficit-in-fy26). This deficit print now sits directly beneath a Brent tape that briefly topped $100/bbl this week -- Pakistan's FY26 oil import bill already ran $16.86bn, $1.58bn above the IMF's programme estimate, before this spike (https://www.nation.com.pk/20-Jul-2026/annual-oil-import-bill-surged-dollar-16-86b-fy2025-26).

global_read: global.json (17:37) shows oil whipsawing hard: Brent $91.88 (-8.75% 1d, +24.6% 1mo) after having crossed $100.69 intraday Thursday for the first time since May -- a sharp round trip, not a resolved shock. VIX is calm at 18.6 (-0.53% 1d) and PKR/DXY are steady (277.67 / 101.45), but S&P -1.21%/Dow -0.97% confirm the global risk tape stayed negative through the week. The oil pullback is real but the underlying supply-chokepoint stress (Hormuz + Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb + now Kazakhstan's CPC Black Sea terminal) is unresolved, and it is landing on a Pakistan current account that just swung back into deficit -- a genuine imported-inflation and reserves risk three days before the 2026-07-27 MPC.
drivers: Brent crude topped $100/bbl for the first time since May 26 (settling near $100.69, +7% on the day) after Houthi forces attacked two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb, before easing back to $91.88 (-8.75% intraday per global.json) into Friday -- still on course for a ~13.5% weekly gain, with a third chokepoint now live after Kazakhstan began cutting CPC pipeline output following drone strikes on its Black Sea export terminal (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/23/oil-prices-today-wti-brent-trump-iran-hormuz.html, https://oilprice.com/Energy/Oil-Prices/Brent-Tops-100-as-Houthi-Attacks-Push-Oil-Rally-Into-Triple-Digits.html, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-23/latest-oil-market-news-and-analysis-for-july-24)

KSE-100 fell for a fourth straight session on 2026-07-24 (Friday), closing at 171,021 (-718pts, -0.42%) after Thursday's -1.54% (-2,690pt) drop -- a cumulative weekly loss of 2.72% (4,782pts) as Middle East tensions kept oil and global borrowing costs elevated and investors stayed risk-off per Arif Habib trading desk commentary (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2619973/psx-continues-to-lose-ground-sheds-1264-points)

Pakistan's FY26 oil import bill already surged to $16.86bn, $1.58bn above the IMF's programme estimate, even before this week's spike -- petroleum imports run ~22% of the total import bill, so a sustained Brent move toward/above $100 is a direct current-account and PKR-defense risk landing on top of June's swing to deficit (https://www.nation.com.pk/20-Jul-2026/annual-oil-import-bill-surged-dollar-16-86b-fy2025-26, https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/20/pakistans-oil-import-bill-exceeds-imf-estimate-in-fy26/)

SBP's 2026-07-27 MPC (3 days out) is still expected to hold at 11.5% even as the conflict escalates -- a Business Recorder poll of analysts published today (2026-07-24) confirms the status-quo call despite the oil rebound, citing well-anchored core inflation against acute geopolitical uncertainty (https://www.brecorder.com/news/amp/40431259, https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/21/sbp-likely-to-keep-interest-rate-unchanged/)

SBP FX reserves held broadly steady at $17.26bn as of 2026-07-17 (+$33mn w/w), with total liquid reserves at $22.67bn -- no fresher reserves print exists yet, so this week's oil spike has not shown up in reserves data (https://pakobserver.net/sbps-foreign-reserves-rise-by-33-million-to-17-26-billion/)

IMF's 4th EFF/RSF review still has no confirmed date; the 3rd EFF review (completed 2026-05-08) disbursed ~$1.1bn of the EFF tranche and the programme remains on track, but there is no fresh review news this run (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf)

Net regime read: the impact-4 oil/conflict shock is confirmed live -- Brent briefly cleared $100 for the first time since May on a THIRD simultaneous chokepoint (Kazakhstan CPC joining Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb) -- and even though oil pulled back sharply intraday Friday and the desk's geo-risk composite eased to 'moderate' (61), the PSX tape itself is the hardest evidence: four consecutive losing KSE-100 sessions and a 2.72% weekly decline, landing on a current account that just swung back into deficit and an oil import bill already running above IMF programme estimates. That combination -- confirmed price action plus an unresolved multi-front energy shock -- keeps the call at risk-off; the S&P upgrade and steady MPC-hold consensus argue against a deeper spiral but do not flip the regime. Regime held at risk-off, unchanged from this morning's pre-shock read but now explicitly reflecting the oil-shock escalation per the impact-4 news trigger.
